question: Should `allowLoopbackHttpWebhook` intentionally stop permitting private HTTPS webhook targets, or must existing private-target harnesses retain an explicit compatibility path?
rationale: The stricter interpretation improves SSRF boundaries but can intentionally break existing configurations, so repository intent—not code correctness alone—must settle the permanent contract.

options.title: Keep the strict boundary
options.body: Retain the HTTP-loopback-only exception and ensure upgrade-facing documentation or PR context clearly identifies that private HTTPS targets are now rejected.

options.title: Add an explicit compatibility control
options.body: Preserve the secure default while providing a narrowly named opt-in for trusted private HTTPS test targets with focused security and upgrade tests.

recommendation.title: Keep the strict boundary
recommendation.body: Retain the HTTP-loopback-only exception and ensure upgrade-facing documentation or PR context clearly identifies that private HTTPS targets are now rejected.

likelyOwner.reason: This repository member owns the coordinated implementation and is best positioned to state whether the narrowed target policy is intentional.
